raw.description:
Position Summary
As a Senior Azure Architect, you will lead the design of DataSpring's Azure platform: the landing zones, networking, identity, resilience, and governance that our healthcare data products run on. DataSpring runs several production platforms in Azure that handle protected health information for health plans and providers nationwide, and we are bringing more of their design and operation in-house from vendors. You will help shape our Azure standards, review vendor designs against them, and stay hands-on enough to prove a design before it is adopted. The ideal candidate has designed enterprise Azure environments end to end in a regulated industry, knows where Azure designs break under real load and real outages, and uses AI tools such as Claude Code to work faster.

This is a full-time, remote, exempt position and reports to the Director, Enterprise Architecture & Infrastructure.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Lead architecture design for Azure platforms and initiatives, and contribute to the target-state architecture set by the Director, including landing zones, management group and subscription design, hub-and-spoke networking, and shared services such as API Management, messaging, and identity.
  • Design for resilience: recommend availability, recovery time, and recovery point targets for each platform, and design and regularly test multi-region and disaster recovery patterns that meet them at a reasonable cost.
  • Develop and apply Azure standards through Azure Policy, reference architectures, and reusable infrastructure-as-code modules (Terraform; Helm for Kubernetes workloads; Bicep a plus).
  • Review designs from implementation vendors and partner teams on assigned projects before build, recommend approval, and hold them to the agreed standards through delivery.
  • Lead network architecture, including private, edge, and global traffic management across regions. Responsible for maintaining DNS, hybrid connectivity, and zero-trust network security and segmentation across projects and environments.
  • Partner with Information Security to meet HIPAA, SOC 2, and HITRUST requirements, with strong controls for PHI, identity and access (Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, privileged access), encryption, and logging.
  • Manage cloud costs for assigned projects within approved budgets (FinOps): tagging and showback, right-sizing, reservations and savings plans, and architecture choices that lower run cost.
  • Design the platform foundations for AI workloads, including Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry capacity, gateways, and secure access patterns.
  • Implement and improve observability practices (LGTM, OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights) so incidents can be detected, diagnosed, and traced to root cause.
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex Azure incidents and lead the design fixes that follow.
  • Mentor engineers on the Architecture and Infrastructure team and raise the team's Azure design skills.
  • Document architecture decisions and maintain current-state and target-state diagrams.
  • Report weekly status on architecture initiatives to designated DataSpring management.
  • Follow all DataSpring Policies and Procedures.

Skills

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in Azure architecture: landing zones, management groups and subscriptions, Azure Policy, and the Cloud Adoption and Well-Architected Frameworks.
  • Strong Azure networking: hub-and-spoke and Virtual WAN, Private Link, Azure DNS, Application Gateway and Front Door, Azure Firewall, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Proven design of multi-region, highly available, and disaster recovery architectures for PaaS and container workloads (App Service, AKS, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Storage).
  • Identity architecture with Microsoft Entra ID across multiple tenants, including managed identities, RBAC, Conditional Access, and privileged access.
  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform required; Bicep a plus) and CI/CD for infrastructure; able to write and review modules, not just specify them.
  • Cloud security in a regulated environment (HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST): encryption, key management, logging, and defense in depth.
  • FinOps practice: reading Azure cost data, forecasting spend, and designing for cost.
  • Ability to explain design trade-offs clearly to engineers, vendors, and executives, and to push back on a vendor design with evidence.
  • Demonstrated use of AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) to accelerate design, infrastructure as code, and analysis.
  • Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, or SAFe delivery is a plus.

Experience & Education

  • 8+ years in infrastructure or cloud engineering, with at least 5 years designing Azure environments at enterprise scale as a cloud or solutions architect.
  • Has led an Azure landing zone or platform design in production, including a disaster recovery design that was tested. Healthcare or other regulated-industry experience (HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST) strongly preferred; experience directing vendor or managed-service delivery teams is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305) strongly preferred; Azure networking or security specialty certifications are a plus.

Who We Are

DataSpring is the trusted data connector at the core of healthcare. For more than 25 years, we have powered the industry with the largest and most complete healthcare data foundation in the U.S., including more than 4.8 million provider data records sourced directly from providers and member data representing 75% of covered lives supplied by health plans. By improving how essential information flows across the system, DataSpring helps healthcare operate more efficiently, accurately, and with greater confidence.

What You Get

At DataSpring, you will do meaningful work at the intersection of healthcare, data, and technology, helping solve complex problems that make the healthcare system work better. You will collaborate with experienced professionals who care deeply about accuracy, trust, and meaningful impact in a fully remote environment.

DataSpring offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company contributions and matching, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and generous paid time off. We are committed to investing in our people and supporting professional growth over time.

Equal Opportunity Employer

DataSpring is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering a workplace where all individuals are valued, respected, and empowered.

Employment decisions at DataSpring are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin or ancestry, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, familial status, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, genetic information, source of income or any other characteristic protected by law. DataSpring does not tolerate unlawful discrimination or harassment of any kind.

Applicants have rights under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA),Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO), and the Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA). If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply for a posted position, please contact the DataSpring People & Culture team at or 202-517-0436.

Position Highlights

Position Title: Project Implementation Manager

Department: Programs and Innovation Office – Workforce Acceleration Initiative

FLSA Classification: Exempt

Reports to: Project Manager - Workforce Acceleration Initiative

Location: Remote, must be based in the United States, Up to 10% domestic travel may be required.

Salary Range: $90,000 - $123,000 per year, plus benefits. Individual salary offers will be based on experience and qualifications unique to each candidate.

Position Type: Grant funded, limited-term opportunity

Position End Date: June 30, 2027

Hours of Work: Individual must routinely be available during core department business hours to collaborate with Illinois Department of Public Health staff.

Overview

The Project Implementation Manager will drive the delivery of data modernization projects that improve the use of public health data to inform decision making. This role is aligned to the Workforce Acceleration Initiative (WAI). WAI is a federally funded CDC Foundation program with the goal of helping the nation’s public health agencies by providing them with the technology and data experts they need to accelerate their information system improvements.

Working within the Illinois Department of Public Health the Project Implementation Manager will collaborate across technical and non-technical teams to define project objectives, allocate resources, coordinate with teams, and manage timelines to ensure the successful delivery and implementation of a public health data systems project.

The Project Implementation Manager will be hired by the CDC Foundation and assigned to the Illinois Department of Public Health. This position is eligible for a fully remote work arrangement for U.S. based candidates.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain data modernization workplans, serving as the Project Implementation Manager to develop detailed project plans and timelines, as well as maintain project documentation including project charters, plans, status reports, and post-project evaluations.
  • Drive project deliverables to ensure they are within scope, deadlines, and budget.
  • Develop and execute supporting plans including data communication, data training, and the data modernization initiative (DMI) evaluation plan. Support execution of enterprise-wide data maturity assessment. Develop and conduct surveys and focus groups as needed to assist in assessment. Create an evaluation plan for data modernization impact analysis. Assist with implementation of the data maturity roadmap.
  • Establish measurable metrics to be used to evaluate DMI activities and impact.
  • Schedule and organize regular recurring meetings with internal and external data interest holders to review project progress, address any issues or concerns, identify data needs and gaps.
  • Schedule and organize data modernization advisory committee meetings.
  • Collaborate with DMI core team including (data governance manager, metadata specialist, data training and communication specialist, business process analyst) to execute DMI workplan. Work with business analysts and other stakeholders to implement and adopt change management strategies.
  • Define clear roles and responsibilities and ensure standards and best practices are followed.
  • Work with user community, technical teams and vendors to meet implementation timeline.
  • Document business practices and workflows, identify opportunities for improvement, support process improvement, discover issues and deliver improved value.
  • Effectively communicating insights and plans to cross-functional team members and management. Facilitate communication between project team members, business analysts, and stakeholders. Create dashboards and generate reports.
  • Develop and implement change management strategies and plans to support the successful adoption and implementation of data modernization transformational activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in project management, public health, information systems, operations management or related field required. Master’s degree or other related advanced degree in a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 10 years of related experience leading data management projects.
  • Expert knowledge of project management fundamentals, including the ability to develop and implement accurate work plans, schedules, staffing plans, and budgets, in an agile or iterative environment. Proficiency in Smartsheet, Confluence, SharePoint and/or other project management tools and techniques.
  • Experienced in change management and risk management principles and processes.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to describe difficult technical problems and solutions to technical and non-technical teams.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining working relationships with internal and external partners and can effectively promote collaboration among differing viewpoints.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and teamwork skills; and the ability to develop productive working relationships with colleagues and partners.
  • Experience working in a virtual environment with remote partners and teams.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
  • Knowledge of data management, data governance and change management.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification or equivalent is preferred.

Special Notes

This role is involved in a dynamic public health program. As such, roles and responsibilities are subject to change as situations evolve. Roles and responsibilities listed above may be expanded upon or updated to match priorities and needs, once written approval is received by the CDC Foundation in order to best support the public health programming.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law.

We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

Relocation expenses are not included.

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. Visit for more information.

raw.description:
Technical Consultant (Pre-Sales)


About the Team

This role sits within Elsevier’s Advanced Data Solutions team, which is responsible for selling and enabling customer implementations of Elsevier’s data and software solutions.

Technical Consultants (Pre-Sales) report to the global Director of Technical Consulting (Pre-Sales) while operating in regionally aligned roles, with ownership across North America, EMEA, and APAC (primarily Japan). The team partners closely with Sales, post-sales, and Professional Services teams to support enterprise customer engagements.


About the Role

As a Technical Consultant (Pre-Sales), you will play a critical role in driving revenue growth by partnering with Sales to position Elsevier’s data and software solutions, and analytics capabilities as enablers of customer insight and decision-making. You will act as the technical authority throughout the sales cycle – leading discovery, shaping data-driven use cases, and demonstrating how Elsevier’s offerings can be combined to power advanced analytics, knowledge graphs, and AI-enabled workflows, including grounding LLMs, agents, and RAG applications in trusted scientific data.


This role focuses mainly on pre-sales activities, with close collaboration across post-sales, professional services, and product teams to ensure proposed solutions are technically feasible, scalable, and aligned with real-world delivery and adoption.


Success in this role is built on a strong technical foundation, practical AI and data expertise, curiosity about scientific domains, and exceptional customer-facing skills, enabling you to translate data and software capabilities into compelling, outcome-driven solutions.


Responsibilities


Pre-sales solution leadership


  • Develop and maintain expertise in Elsevier’s solutions, including curated datasets, data APIs and integration options, MCP servers, AI agents, and SciBite semantic solutions, and how these combine to give customers' analytics and AI applications trusted access to Elsevier data and deliver insights.
  • Lead technical discovery to understand customer objectives, analytical workflows, data landscapes, and success criteria, translating business and scientific challenges into data-driven use cases, solution architectures, and value narratives
  • Design and deliver tailored solution demonstrations showcasing how Elsevier data and software enable insights (e.g., discovery, analytics, AI-powered workflows and agents, and knowledge graph construction).
  • Scope and prepare solution proposals, and support proof-of-concepts (PoCs), technical evaluations, and pilots to validate solution fit and value, clearly articulating technical trade-offs, assumptions, and dependencies across data, software, and services.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the sales cycle, supporting account strategy, solution positioning, and competitive differentiation.
  • Stay current with developments in AI (e.g., LLMs, agentic workflows, and responsible AI) and advise customers on how to apply them with Elsevier data, while using AI tools to improve the speed and quality of pre-sales work such as demos, proposals, and PoCs.

Cross-functional alignment

  • Validate solution feasibility in collaboration with Product and Professional Services teams to ensure smooth delivery, adoption, and account growth and expansion.
  • Capture customer feedback and market insights to inform product positioning, roadmap priorities, and go-to-market strategy in partnership with Product and Marketing teams.

Requirements


  • Have deepp understanding of data-driven analytics workflows, including data ingestion, enrichment, integration, and insight generation
  • Have working knowledge of Generative AI and LLM-based solutions (e.g., RAG, prompt design, agentic workflows, evaluation, and responsible AI and data governance), and of how NER, ontologies, taxonomies, and knowledge graphs are applied to real-world analytical use cases
  • Have working knowledge of cloud and technical ecosystems (e.g., AWS, REST APIs, SFTP, HTTP, OAuth, Docker, Python, etc.), with familiarity with AI platforms, tooling, and integration patterns (e.g., LLM APIs, MCP).
  • Have a degree in a science, technology, or data field (Master’s or PhD advantageous), or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience working in data-intensive enterprise environments (e.g., technology, engineering, pharma, or life sciences); life sciences experience is desirable but not essential, alongside a willingness to learn scientific domains.
  • Have an understanding of how data and software are used to support research, analytics, and decision-making is highly valued.
  • Experience delivering technical demonstrations and presentations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Excellent communication, storytelling, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Display confidence leading complex technical discussions and navigating challenging or ambiguous customer conversations
  • Able to travel to customer sites and industry events as required.

Work in a Way That Works for You
We promote a healthy work-life balance and offer flexible working options. Our benefits include wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals—supporting both your immediate responsibilities and long-term goals.


Working for You
We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:

Health benefits: medical, dental, and vision coverage
Retirement benefits: 401(k) with match and Employee Share Purchase Plan
Wellbeing: wellness platform, Headspace subscription, and Employee Assistance Programs
Insurance: short- and long-term disability, life, accidental death, critical illness, and hospital indemnity
Family benefits: parental leave, adoption, and surrogacy support
Savings accounts: HSA, FSA, dependent care, and commuter benefits
Paid time off, plus volunteer and Employee Resource Group participation days

About the Business
As a global leader in information and analytics, we help researchers and healthcare professionals advance science and improve health outcomes. By combining trusted content with advanced analytics, we support research, education, and clinical practice. At Elsevier, your work contributes to solving global challenges and building a more sustainable future.

raw.description:
Job Description

Optimum Energy is looking for a smart, motivated, collaborative business professional to join our accounting team as a Staff Accountant, reporting to the Controller. The Staff Accountant will own the day-to-day accounts payable process, including invoice review and approval support, the weekly check run, and vendor statement reconciliations. This role will also prepare journal entries and reconciliations for accruals, accounts payable, bank accounts, and the balance sheet as part of month-end close, code and enter monthly credit card receipts into NetSuite, and assist with monthly state sales tax filings and financial audit requests. The ideal candidate is comfortable building and maintaining Excel spreadsheets for ad hoc projects and tracking, and is ready to support the Senior Accountant and Controller on special projects as needed. Success attributes critical to this role include initiative, creativity, curiosity, and desire to tackle big challenges.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Accounts Payable: Review invoices for proper support and approval. Assist with weekly check run processes. Reconcile vendor statements to ensure proper balances.
  • Month-End Close: Reconcile accruals and accounts payable and prepare journal entries. Reconcile bank accounts and maintain balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Fixed Assets: Maintain fixed asset registers and calculate monthly depreciation.
  • Credit Card & Expense Reporting: Collect monthly credit card receipts, code them, and enter them into NetSuite. Assist with expense report tracking and coding.
  • Tax & Audit Support: Assist with monthly state sales tax filings and financial audit requests.
  • Special Projects: Assist with special projects and work alongside the Senior Accountant. Create and maintain Excel spreadsheets for various projects and tracking purposes.

Key Competencies and Skills Expectations

  • Integrity: High level of integrity, trust, and the ability to maintain confidentiality is critical.
  • Problem Solving: Effective problem-solving abilities.
  • Customer Service: Professional, yet personal demeanor and strong customer service skills.
  • Communication: Good verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Organization & Time Management: Ability to multi-task, meet deadlines, handle frequent interruptions, and maintain a high level of productivity.
  • Attention to Detail: Accuracy and careful attention to detail required. Produces high-quality work.
  • Results Focus: Focus on results and success, conveying a sense of urgency and seeing issues through to closure.

Requirements

  • Education: 4-year bachelor's degree in Accounting preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 1 to 2 years of accounting and/or accounts payable experience.
    • Knowledge of basic accounting principles including AR, AP, accruals, and general ledger.
    • Working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) preferred.
  • Technical Knowledge: Intermediate to advanced Excel skills. Intermediate experience with NetSuite preferred. Knowledge of MS Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint) and SharePoint (preferred).

Optimum Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer encouraging diversity in the workplace.

About the Company

Optimum Energy, a Bernhard Capital Partners portfolio company, has spent 20 years helping hospitals, universities, government facilities, and advanced manufacturing operations reduce energy consumption

in heating and cooling systems by up to 50% and turn that infrastructure into a strategic financial and

operational asset. With 300+ plants and institutions served globally, nobody understands energy

infrastructure, efficiency, and financial opportunity quite like Optimum Energy.

Our Energy-as-a-Service model converts aging central utility plants into upfront unrestricted cash, cuts utility operating expenses 25 to 35%, and keeps the transaction entirely off the balance sheet. The structure has been confirmed by Big Four auditors and cited by rating agencies as a driver of improved credit outlooks.

We work with clients from master planning and design through implementation, commissioning, and into long-term operations and maintenance. How we show up depends on what the client needs. That could

mean fully managed plants with Optimum carrying total accountability for performance and uptime. It

could mean supplementing an existing facilities team with engineering support, analytics, training, and escalation resources. Or it could mean a tailored combination of both. In every engagement, we stay for

the life of the agreement.

Proprietary technology, including OptiCx and OptimumLOOP, powers everything we do. It is not what we sell. It is what enables us to deliver the most continuous, precise system-level optimization across chilled water, hot water, and steam plants available in the market today. Machine learning algorithms trained on two decades of operational data adapt to load, weather, and occupancy in real time. AI-driven predictive maintenance and fault detection catch equipment degradation before it becomes a problem. We guarantee the performance. We carry the risk.

Behind the technology is a team built on a simple set of principles: be sharp, be relentless, and be accountable for outcomes. Our people are engineers, operators, and financial structurers who would rather solve the hard problem than talk around it. Every engagement gets that same intensity, whether the scope is a single plant or a 26-site enterprise portfolio. For more information, visit .

About the Industry

Commercial and institutional HVAC infrastructure is aging faster than organizations can replace it. Hospitals are running central plants built in the 1960s and 70s. Universities carry over $112 billion in

collective deferred maintenance nationally. Advanced manufacturing operations face intensifying energy demand from reshoring and facility expansion. Rising energy costs, tightening regulations, sustainability mandates, and a skilled trades labor gap that shows no sign of closing all compound the pressure.

Connected systems are generating more data than most organizations can act on. The capacity to analyze it and translate it into operational decisions requires platforms and people most facilities teams do not have. The industry is not short on ambition or technology. It is short on the capital structures, operational models, and workforce capacity to turn intent into sustained results.

Why Optimum Energy?

With 300+ sites and over 300M square feet of operational data, our machine learning algorithms

continuously optimize in real time. No competitor replicates this at scale.

We do not sell software, and we do not sell equipment. We deliver guaranteed outcomes through the convergence of deep engineering expertise, proprietary optimization technology, and financial structures that align our interests directly with those of our clients. That means tailoring solutions to unique financial and operational realities, not forcing a one-size-fits-all model. It means verifiable success across facility design, ongoing operations, and complex deal structuring. And it means protecting client investments by optimizing the 70% of total costs that occur after day one.

Our EaaS contracts transfer construction, performance, and lifecycle risk entirely. No upfront capital. No balance sheet impact. Capital that would have gone to back-of-house infrastructure stays available for the priorities that matter most, whether that is clinical growth, enrollment expansion, or production capacity.

No other firm brings this combination of engineering, technology, operations, and financial structuring under a single partnership.

Salary: $75,000 - $85,000

raw.description:
Build and run the GHL systems that turn leads into members and keep members coming back — and be the go-to support for the gym team using them.

About the Role

Seamless Assist places AI-fluent virtual assistants with growing businesses and builds the automation systems they run. We are hiring a GoHighLevel Specialist on behalf of our client, a US-based gym business. This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in Mexico.

The gym runs its lead follow-up, trial bookings, member communication, and retention campaigns through GoHighLevel. This hire owns that platform end to end — building the automations that drive memberships and supporting the owner and front-desk team who use it every day.

Culture: owner-led, fast-moving fitness business. Clear ownership, proactive communication, and steady improvement over perfection.

Role Details

  • Industry: Health & Fitness — Gym
  • Reports to: Gym Owner
  • Type: Full-time · 40 hours/week
  • Hours: US Eastern Time (EST) business hours
  • Rate: TBD
  • Location: Remote — Mexico
  • Tools: GoHighLevel (GHL), Zapier / Make / n8n, gym management software (e.g., Mindbody, ABC Glofox, PushPress, Zen Planner), Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Google Workspace

Role Overview

Every lead, trial, and member touchpoint at the gym runs through GoHighLevel. The GHL Specialist will design and maintain those systems — from the first ad inquiry to the membership renewal — and provide responsive, first-line support to the gym owner and staff.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move between building and supporting in the same day: fixing a broken trial-booking workflow in the morning, walking the front desk through the pipeline after lunch, and documenting both so it doesn't happen twice. The right person treats every support request as a signal of what to systematize next.

Key Responsibilities

GHL Automation & Build

  • Build and maintain lead nurture workflows — speed-to-lead SMS/email, trial class and intro session booking, and follow-up for leads who don't book
  • Automate the member journey — class and appointment reminders, no-show follow-up, new-member onboarding, and milestone check-ins
  • Run retention and reactivation campaigns — lapsed and frozen members, expiring memberships, failed payments, and win-back offers
  • Set up and manage pipelines, calendars, forms, surveys, landing pages/funnels, custom fields, and tags
  • Build and send email and SMS campaigns — promotions, challenges, events, and monthly member newsletters
  • Automate review requests and referral campaigns to grow the gym's reputation
  • Integrate GHL with the gym's management software, payment tools, and ad lead sources (Facebook/Instagram lead forms) via native integrations, Zapier, Make, n8n, or webhooks

Customer Support

  • Serve as first-line GHL support for the gym owner and front-desk/sales staff
  • Manage and respond to member and lead inquiries in the GHL Conversations inbox (SMS, email, social DMs) within agreed response times
  • Troubleshoot issues: broken workflows, failed sends, calendar sync errors, A2P/10DLC and email deliverability problems, integration failures
  • Train gym staff on using GHL — pipelines, conversations, booking, and reporting — through live walkthroughs and short recorded videos
  • Escalate billing, platform-level bugs, or out-of-scope requests to the gym owner with a clear summary

Reporting, Documentation & Improvement

  • Build dashboards that track leads, trial bookings, show rates, conversions to membership, and retention
  • Write SOPs and how-to guides for every recurring build and support issue
  • Audit the account for broken, duplicate, or unused workflows and recommend clean-up
  • Track recurring issues and propose automations or fixes that remove them at the source
  • Use AI tools to speed up campaign copy, troubleshooting, and documentation

Who Will Succeed

"Builds it right, explains it simply, and fixes the root cause — not just the ticket."

  • Has built real GHL automations for live businesses — ideally gyms, studios, or other membership businesses
  • Understands how a gym makes money: leads, trials, memberships, retention
  • Patient and clear with busy, non-technical owners and staff — explains a workflow without jargon
  • Systems thinker who documents as they go and hates fixing the same problem twice
  • Takes initiative — spots what is broken or missing and raises it before the owner does

Experience & Skills

Required

  • GHL expertise: 2+ years of hands-on GoHighLevel experience building workflows, pipelines, funnels, and campaigns for live businesses
  • Customer support: 1+ year providing customer or technical support (tickets, live chat, calls, or client success)
  • Integrations: Working knowledge of Zapier, Make, n8n, or webhooks to connect GHL with other tools
  • AI fluency: Actively uses AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) to build, write, and troubleshoot faster — specific tools and use cases confirmed at screening
  • Time zone compatibility: Able to work US Eastern Time (EST) business hours from Mexico
  • Strong communication: Exceptional written and spoken English — clear, friendly, and concise with owners, staff, and members; assessed at screening
  • Deliverability: Understanding of email and SMS deliverability, including A2P 10DLC registration
  • Remote setup: Reliable high-speed internet and a dedicated workspace

Preferred

  • Experience with gyms, fitness studios, or other membership-based businesses
  • Experience with gym management software (Mindbody, ABC Glofox, PushPress, Zen Planner, or similar)
  • GHL Admin certification
  • Familiarity with GHL Conversation AI / AI Employee features
  • Experience running Facebook/Instagram lead-gen campaigns into GHL

Position Highlights

Position Title: Project Implementation Manager

Department: Programs and Innovation Office – Workforce Acceleration Initiative

FLSA Classification: Exempt

Reports to: Project Manager - Workforce Acceleration Initiative

Location: Remote, must be based in the United States, Up to 10% domestic travel may be required.

Salary Range: $90,000 - $123,000 per year, plus benefits. Individual salary offers will be based on experience and qualifications unique to each candidate.

Position Type: Grant funded, limited-term opportunity

Position End Date: June 30, 2027

Hours of Work: Individual must routinely be available during core department business hours to collaborate with Illinois Department of Public Health staff.

Overview

The Project Implementation Manager will drive the delivery of data modernization projects that improve the use of public health data to inform decision making. This role is aligned to the Workforce Acceleration Initiative (WAI). WAI is a federally funded CDC Foundation program with the goal of helping the nation’s public health agencies by providing them with the technology and data experts they need to accelerate their information system improvements.

Working within the Illinois Department of Public Health the Project Implementation Manager will collaborate across technical and non-technical teams to define project objectives, allocate resources, coordinate with teams, and manage timelines to ensure the successful delivery and implementation of a public health data systems project.

The Project Implementation Manager will be hired by the CDC Foundation and assigned to the Illinois Department of Public Health. This position is eligible for a fully remote work arrangement for U.S. based candidates.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain data modernization workplans, serving as the Project Implementation Manager to develop detailed project plans and timelines, as well as maintain project documentation including project charters, plans, status reports, and post-project evaluations.
  • Drive project deliverables to ensure they are within scope, deadlines, and budget.
  • Develop and execute supporting plans including data communication, data training, and the data modernization initiative (DMI) evaluation plan. Support execution of enterprise-wide data maturity assessment. Develop and conduct surveys and focus groups as needed to assist in assessment. Create an evaluation plan for data modernization impact analysis. Assist with implementation of the data maturity roadmap.
  • Establish measurable metrics to be used to evaluate DMI activities and impact.
  • Schedule and organize regular recurring meetings with internal and external data interest holders to review project progress, address any issues or concerns, identify data needs and gaps.
  • Schedule and organize data modernization advisory committee meetings.
  • Collaborate with DMI core team including (data governance manager, metadata specialist, data training and communication specialist, business process analyst) to execute DMI workplan. Work with business analysts and other stakeholders to implement and adopt change management strategies.
  • Define clear roles and responsibilities and ensure standards and best practices are followed.
  • Work with user community, technical teams and vendors to meet implementation timeline.
  • Document business practices and workflows, identify opportunities for improvement, support process improvement, discover issues and deliver improved value.
  • Effectively communicating insights and plans to cross-functional team members and management. Facilitate communication between project team members, business analysts, and stakeholders. Create dashboards and generate reports.
  • Develop and implement change management strategies and plans to support the successful adoption and implementation of data modernization transformational activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in project management, public health, information systems, operations management or related field required. Master’s degree or other related advanced degree in a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 10 years of related experience leading data management projects.
  • Expert knowledge of project management fundamentals, including the ability to develop and implement accurate work plans, schedules, staffing plans, and budgets, in an agile or iterative environment. Proficiency in Smartsheet, Confluence, SharePoint and/or other project management tools and techniques.
  • Experienced in change management and risk management principles and processes.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to describe difficult technical problems and solutions to technical and non-technical teams.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining working relationships with internal and external partners and can effectively promote collaboration among differing viewpoints.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and teamwork skills; and the ability to develop productive working relationships with colleagues and partners.
  • Experience working in a virtual environment with remote partners and teams.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
  • Knowledge of data management, data governance and change management.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification or equivalent is preferred.

Special Notes

This role is involved in a dynamic public health program. As such, roles and responsibilities are subject to change as situations evolve. Roles and responsibilities listed above may be expanded upon or updated to match priorities and needs, once written approval is received by the CDC Foundation in order to best support the public health programming.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law.

We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

Position Summary
As a Senior Azure Architect, you will lead the design of DataSpring's Azure platform: the landing zones, networking, identity, resilience, and governance that our healthcare data products run on. DataSpring runs several production platforms in Azure that handle protected health information for health plans and providers nationwide, and we are bringing more of their design and operation in-house from vendors. You will help shape our Azure standards, review vendor designs against them, and stay hands-on enough to prove a design before it is adopted. The ideal candidate has designed enterprise Azure environments end to end in a regulated industry, knows where Azure designs break under real load and real outages, and uses AI tools such as Claude Code to work faster.

This is a full-time, remote, exempt position and reports to the Director, Enterprise Architecture & Infrastructure.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Lead architecture design for Azure platforms and initiatives, and contribute to the target-state architecture set by the Director, including landing zones, management group and subscription design, hub-and-spoke networking, and shared services such as API Management, messaging, and identity.
  • Design for resilience: recommend availability, recovery time, and recovery point targets for each platform, and design and regularly test multi-region and disaster recovery patterns that meet them at a reasonable cost.
  • Develop and apply Azure standards through Azure Policy, reference architectures, and reusable infrastructure-as-code modules (Terraform; Helm for Kubernetes workloads; Bicep a plus).
  • Review designs from implementation vendors and partner teams on assigned projects before build, recommend approval, and hold them to the agreed standards through delivery.
  • Lead network architecture, including private, edge, and global traffic management across regions. Responsible for maintaining DNS, hybrid connectivity, and zero-trust network security and segmentation across projects and environments.
  • Partner with Information Security to meet HIPAA, SOC 2, and HITRUST requirements, with strong controls for PHI, identity and access (Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, privileged access), encryption, and logging.
  • Manage cloud costs for assigned projects within approved budgets (FinOps): tagging and showback, right-sizing, reservations and savings plans, and architecture choices that lower run cost.
  • Design the platform foundations for AI workloads, including Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry capacity, gateways, and secure access patterns.
  • Implement and improve observability practices (LGTM, OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights) so incidents can be detected, diagnosed, and traced to root cause.
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex Azure incidents and lead the design fixes that follow.
  • Mentor engineers on the Architecture and Infrastructure team and raise the team's Azure design skills.
  • Document architecture decisions and maintain current-state and target-state diagrams.
  • Report weekly status on architecture initiatives to designated DataSpring management.
  • Follow all DataSpring Policies and Procedures.

Skills

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in Azure architecture: landing zones, management groups and subscriptions, Azure Policy, and the Cloud Adoption and Well-Architected Frameworks.
  • Strong Azure networking: hub-and-spoke and Virtual WAN, Private Link, Azure DNS, Application Gateway and Front Door, Azure Firewall, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Proven design of multi-region, highly available, and disaster recovery architectures for PaaS and container workloads (App Service, AKS, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Storage).
  • Identity architecture with Microsoft Entra ID across multiple tenants, including managed identities, RBAC, Conditional Access, and privileged access.
  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform required; Bicep a plus) and CI/CD for infrastructure; able to write and review modules, not just specify them.
  • Cloud security in a regulated environment (HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST): encryption, key management, logging, and defense in depth.
  • FinOps practice: reading Azure cost data, forecasting spend, and designing for cost.
  • Ability to explain design trade-offs clearly to engineers, vendors, and executives, and to push back on a vendor design with evidence.
  • Demonstrated use of AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) to accelerate design, infrastructure as code, and analysis.
  • Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, or SAFe delivery is a plus.

Experience & Education

  • 8+ years in infrastructure or cloud engineering, with at least 5 years designing Azure environments at enterprise scale as a cloud or solutions architect.
  • Has led an Azure landing zone or platform design in production, including a disaster recovery design that was tested. Healthcare or other regulated-industry experience (HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST) strongly preferred; experience directing vendor or managed-service delivery teams is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305) strongly preferred; Azure networking or security specialty certifications are a plus.

Who We Are

DataSpring is the trusted data connector at the core of healthcare. For more than 25 years, we have powered the industry with the largest and most complete healthcare data foundation in the U.S., including more than 4.8 million provider data records sourced directly from providers and member data representing 75% of covered lives supplied by health plans. By improving how essential information flows across the system, DataSpring helps healthcare operate more efficiently, accurately, and with greater confidence.

What You Get

At DataSpring, you will do meaningful work at the intersection of healthcare, data, and technology, helping solve complex problems that make the healthcare system work better. You will collaborate with experienced professionals who care deeply about accuracy, trust, and meaningful impact in a fully remote environment.

DataSpring offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company contributions and matching, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and generous paid time off. We are committed to investing in our people and supporting professional growth over time.

Equal Opportunity Employer

DataSpring is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering a workplace where all individuals are valued, respected, and empowered.

Employment decisions at DataSpring are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin or ancestry, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, familial status, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, genetic information, source of income or any other characteristic protected by law. DataSpring does not tolerate unlawful discrimination or harassment of any kind.

Applicants have rights under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA),Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO), and the Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA). If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply for a posted position, please contact the DataSpring People & Culture team at or 202-517-0436.

Position Title: Project Implementation Manager

Department: Programs and Innovation Office – Workforce Acceleration Initiative

Hours of Work: Individual must routinely be available during core department business hours to collaborate with Illinois Department of Public Health staff.

Overview

The Project Implementation Manager will drive the delivery of data modernization projects that improve the use of public health data to inform decision making. This role is aligned to the Workforce Acceleration Initiative (WAI). WAI is a federally funded CDC Foundation program with the goal of helping the nation’s public health agencies by providing them with the technology and data experts they need to accelerate their information system improvements.

Working within the Illinois Department of Public Health the Project Implementation Manager will collaborate across technical and non-technical teams to define project objectives, allocate resources, coordinate with teams, and manage timelines to ensure the successful delivery and implementation of a public health data systems project.

The Project Implementation Manager will be hired by the CDC Foundation and assigned to the Illinois Department of Public Health. This position is eligible for a fully remote work arrangement for U.S. based candidates.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain data modernization workplans, serving as the Project Implementation Manager to develop detailed project plans and timelines, as well as maintain project documentation including project charters, plans, status reports, and post-project evaluations.
  • Drive project deliverables to ensure they are within scope, deadlines, and budget.
  • Develop and execute supporting plans including data communication, data training, and the data modernization initiative (DMI) evaluation plan. Support execution of enterprise-wide data maturity assessment. Develop and conduct surveys and focus groups as needed to assist in assessment. Create an evaluation plan for data modernization impact analysis. Assist with implementation of the data maturity roadmap.
  • Establish measurable metrics to be used to evaluate DMI activities and impact.
  • Schedule and organize regular recurring meetings with internal and external data interest holders to review project progress, address any issues or concerns, identify data needs and gaps.
  • Schedule and organize data modernization advisory committee meetings.
  • Collaborate with DMI core team including (data governance manager, metadata specialist, data training and communication specialist, business process analyst) to execute DMI workplan. Work with business analysts and other stakeholders to implement and adopt change management strategies.
  • Define clear roles and responsibilities and ensure standards and best practices are followed.
  • Work with user community, technical teams and vendors to meet implementation timeline.
  • Document business practices and workflows, identify opportunities for improvement, support process improvement, discover issues and deliver improved value.
  • Effectively communicating insights and plans to cross-functional team members and management. Facilitate communication between project team members, business analysts, and stakeholders. Create dashboards and generate reports.
  • Develop and implement change management strategies and plans to support the successful adoption and implementation of data modernization transformational activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in project management, public health, information systems, operations management or related field required. Master’s degree or other related advanced degree in a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 10 years of related experience leading data management projects.
  • Expert knowledge of project management fundamentals, including the ability to develop and implement accurate work plans, schedules, staffing plans, and budgets, in an agile or iterative environment. Proficiency in Smartsheet, Confluence, SharePoint and/or other project management tools and techniques.
  • Experienced in change management and risk management principles and processes.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to describe difficult technical problems and solutions to technical and non-technical teams.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining working relationships with internal and external partners and can effectively promote collaboration among differing viewpoints.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and teamwork skills; and the ability to develop productive working relationships with colleagues and partners.
  • Experience working in a virtual environment with remote partners and teams.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
  • Knowledge of data management, data governance and change management.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification or equivalent is preferred.

Special Notes

This role is involved in a dynamic public health program. As such, roles and responsibilities are subject to change as situations evolve. Roles and responsibilities listed above may be expanded upon or updated to match priorities and needs, once written approval is received by the CDC Foundation in order to best support the public health programming.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law.

We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

Relocation expenses are not included.

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. Visit for more information.

Technical Consultant (Pre-Sales)


About the Team

This role sits within Elsevier’s Advanced Data Solutions team, which is responsible for selling and enabling customer implementations of Elsevier’s data and software solutions.

Technical Consultants (Pre-Sales) report to the global Director of Technical Consulting (Pre-Sales) while operating in regionally aligned roles, with ownership across North America, EMEA, and APAC (primarily Japan). The team partners closely with Sales, post-sales, and Professional Services teams to support enterprise customer engagements.


About the Role

As a Technical Consultant (Pre-Sales), you will play a critical role in driving revenue growth by partnering with Sales to position Elsevier’s data and software solutions, and analytics capabilities as enablers of customer insight and decision-making. You will act as the technical authority throughout the sales cycle – leading discovery, shaping data-driven use cases, and demonstrating how Elsevier’s offerings can be combined to power advanced analytics, knowledge graphs, and AI-enabled workflows, including grounding LLMs, agents, and RAG applications in trusted scientific data.


This role focuses mainly on pre-sales activities, with close collaboration across post-sales, professional services, and product teams to ensure proposed solutions are technically feasible, scalable, and aligned with real-world delivery and adoption.


Success in this role is built on a strong technical foundation, practical AI and data expertise, curiosity about scientific domains, and exceptional customer-facing skills, enabling you to translate data and software capabilities into compelling, outcome-driven solutions.


Responsibilities


Pre-sales solution leadership


  • Develop and maintain expertise in Elsevier’s solutions, including curated datasets, data APIs and integration options, MCP servers, AI agents, and SciBite semantic solutions, and how these combine to give customers' analytics and AI applications trusted access to Elsevier data and deliver insights.
  • Lead technical discovery to understand customer objectives, analytical workflows, data landscapes, and success criteria, translating business and scientific challenges into data-driven use cases, solution architectures, and value narratives
  • Design and deliver tailored solution demonstrations showcasing how Elsevier data and software enable insights (e.g., discovery, analytics, AI-powered workflows and agents, and knowledge graph construction).
  • Scope and prepare solution proposals, and support proof-of-concepts (PoCs), technical evaluations, and pilots to validate solution fit and value, clearly articulating technical trade-offs, assumptions, and dependencies across data, software, and services.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the sales cycle, supporting account strategy, solution positioning, and competitive differentiation.
  • Stay current with developments in AI (e.g., LLMs, agentic workflows, and responsible AI) and advise customers on how to apply them with Elsevier data, while using AI tools to improve the speed and quality of pre-sales work such as demos, proposals, and PoCs.

Cross-functional alignment

  • Validate solution feasibility in collaboration with Product and Professional Services teams to ensure smooth delivery, adoption, and account growth and expansion.
  • Capture customer feedback and market insights to inform product positioning, roadmap priorities, and go-to-market strategy in partnership with Product and Marketing teams.

Requirements


  • Have deepp understanding of data-driven analytics workflows, including data ingestion, enrichment, integration, and insight generation
  • Have working knowledge of Generative AI and LLM-based solutions (e.g., RAG, prompt design, agentic workflows, evaluation, and responsible AI and data governance), and of how NER, ontologies, taxonomies, and knowledge graphs are applied to real-world analytical use cases
  • Have working knowledge of cloud and technical ecosystems (e.g., AWS, REST APIs, SFTP, HTTP, OAuth, Docker, Python, etc.), with familiarity with AI platforms, tooling, and integration patterns (e.g., LLM APIs, MCP).
  • Have a degree in a science, technology, or data field (Master’s or PhD advantageous), or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience working in data-intensive enterprise environments (e.g., technology, engineering, pharma, or life sciences); life sciences experience is desirable but not essential, alongside a willingness to learn scientific domains.
  • Have an understanding of how data and software are used to support research, analytics, and decision-making is highly valued.
  • Experience delivering technical demonstrations and presentations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Excellent communication, storytelling, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Display confidence leading complex technical discussions and navigating challenging or ambiguous customer conversations
  • Able to travel to customer sites and industry events as required.

Work in a Way That Works for You
We promote a healthy work-life balance and offer flexible working options. Our benefits include wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals—supporting both your immediate responsibilities and long-term goals.


Working for You
We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:

Health benefits: medical, dental, and vision coverage
Retirement benefits: 401(k) with match and Employee Share Purchase Plan
Wellbeing: wellness platform, Headspace subscription, and Employee Assistance Programs
Insurance: short- and long-term disability, life, accidental death, critical illness, and hospital indemnity
Family benefits: parental leave, adoption, and surrogacy support
Savings accounts: HSA, FSA, dependent care, and commuter benefits
Paid time off, plus volunteer and Employee Resource Group participation days

About the Business
As a global leader in information and analytics, we help researchers and healthcare professionals advance science and improve health outcomes. By combining trusted content with advanced analytics, we support research, education, and clinical practice. At Elsevier, your work contributes to solving global challenges and building a more sustainable future.

raw.description:
Job Description

Optimum Energy is looking for a smart, motivated, collaborative business professional to join our accounting team as a Staff Accountant, reporting to the Controller. The Staff Accountant will own the day-to-day accounts payable process, including invoice review and approval support, the weekly check run, and vendor statement reconciliations. This role will also prepare journal entries and reconciliations for accruals, accounts payable, bank accounts, and the balance sheet as part of month-end close, code and enter monthly credit card receipts into NetSuite, and assist with monthly state sales tax filings and financial audit requests. The ideal candidate is comfortable building and maintaining Excel spreadsheets for ad hoc projects and tracking, and is ready to support the Senior Accountant and Controller on special projects as needed. Success attributes critical to this role include initiative, creativity, curiosity, and desire to tackle big challenges.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Accounts Payable: Review invoices for proper support and approval. Assist with weekly check run processes. Reconcile vendor statements to ensure proper balances.
  • Month-End Close: Reconcile accruals and accounts payable and prepare journal entries. Reconcile bank accounts and maintain balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Fixed Assets: Maintain fixed asset registers and calculate monthly depreciation.
  • Credit Card & Expense Reporting: Collect monthly credit card receipts, code them, and enter them into NetSuite. Assist with expense report tracking and coding.
  • Tax & Audit Support: Assist with monthly state sales tax filings and financial audit requests.
  • Special Projects: Assist with special projects and work alongside the Senior Accountant. Create and maintain Excel spreadsheets for various projects and tracking purposes.

Key Competencies and Skills Expectations

  • Integrity: High level of integrity, trust, and the ability to maintain confidentiality is critical.
  • Problem Solving: Effective problem-solving abilities.
  • Customer Service: Professional, yet personal demeanor and strong customer service skills.
  • Communication: Good verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Organization & Time Management: Ability to multi-task, meet deadlines, handle frequent interruptions, and maintain a high level of productivity.
  • Attention to Detail: Accuracy and careful attention to detail required. Produces high-quality work.
  • Results Focus: Focus on results and success, conveying a sense of urgency and seeing issues through to closure.

Requirements

  • Education: 4-year bachelor's degree in Accounting preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 1 to 2 years of accounting and/or accounts payable experience.
    • Knowledge of basic accounting principles including AR, AP, accruals, and general ledger.
    • Working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) preferred.
  • Technical Knowledge: Intermediate to advanced Excel skills. Intermediate experience with NetSuite preferred. Knowledge of MS Office (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint) and SharePoint (preferred).

Optimum Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer encouraging diversity in the workplace.

About the Company

Optimum Energy, a Bernhard Capital Partners portfolio company, has spent 20 years helping hospitals, universities, government facilities, and advanced manufacturing operations reduce energy consumption

in heating and cooling systems by up to 50% and turn that infrastructure into a strategic financial and

operational asset. With 300+ plants and institutions served globally, nobody understands energy

infrastructure, efficiency, and financial opportunity quite like Optimum Energy.

Our Energy-as-a-Service model converts aging central utility plants into upfront unrestricted cash, cuts utility operating expenses 25 to 35%, and keeps the transaction entirely off the balance sheet. The structure has been confirmed by Big Four auditors and cited by rating agencies as a driver of improved credit outlooks.

We work with clients from master planning and design through implementation, commissioning, and into long-term operations and maintenance. How we show up depends on what the client needs. That could

mean fully managed plants with Optimum carrying total accountability for performance and uptime. It

could mean supplementing an existing facilities team with engineering support, analytics, training, and escalation resources. Or it could mean a tailored combination of both. In every engagement, we stay for

the life of the agreement.

Proprietary technology, including OptiCx and OptimumLOOP, powers everything we do. It is not what we sell. It is what enables us to deliver the most continuous, precise system-level optimization across chilled water, hot water, and steam plants available in the market today. Machine learning algorithms trained on two decades of operational data adapt to load, weather, and occupancy in real time. AI-driven predictive maintenance and fault detection catch equipment degradation before it becomes a problem. We guarantee the performance. We carry the risk.

Behind the technology is a team built on a simple set of principles: be sharp, be relentless, and be accountable for outcomes. Our people are engineers, operators, and financial structurers who would rather solve the hard problem than talk around it. Every engagement gets that same intensity, whether the scope is a single plant or a 26-site enterprise portfolio. For more information, visit .

About the Industry

Commercial and institutional HVAC infrastructure is aging faster than organizations can replace it. Hospitals are running central plants built in the 1960s and 70s. Universities carry over $112 billion in

collective deferred maintenance nationally. Advanced manufacturing operations face intensifying energy demand from reshoring and facility expansion. Rising energy costs, tightening regulations, sustainability mandates, and a skilled trades labor gap that shows no sign of closing all compound the pressure.

Connected systems are generating more data than most organizations can act on. The capacity to analyze it and translate it into operational decisions requires platforms and people most facilities teams do not have. The industry is not short on ambition or technology. It is short on the capital structures, operational models, and workforce capacity to turn intent into sustained results.

Why Optimum Energy?

With 300+ sites and over 300M square feet of operational data, our machine learning algorithms

continuously optimize in real time. No competitor replicates this at scale.

We do not sell software, and we do not sell equipment. We deliver guaranteed outcomes through the convergence of deep engineering expertise, proprietary optimization technology, and financial structures that align our interests directly with those of our clients. That means tailoring solutions to unique financial and operational realities, not forcing a one-size-fits-all model. It means verifiable success across facility design, ongoing operations, and complex deal structuring. And it means protecting client investments by optimizing the 70% of total costs that occur after day one.

Our EaaS contracts transfer construction, performance, and lifecycle risk entirely. No upfront capital. No balance sheet impact. Capital that would have gone to back-of-house infrastructure stays available for the priorities that matter most, whether that is clinical growth, enrollment expansion, or production capacity.

No other firm brings this combination of engineering, technology, operations, and financial structuring under a single partnership.

Salary: $75,000 - $85,000

raw.description:
Build and run the GHL systems that turn leads into members and keep members coming back — and be the go-to support for the gym team using them.

About the Role

Seamless Assist places AI-fluent virtual assistants with growing businesses and builds the automation systems they run. We are hiring a GoHighLevel Specialist on behalf of our client, a US-based gym business. This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in Mexico.

The gym runs its lead follow-up, trial bookings, member communication, and retention campaigns through GoHighLevel. This hire owns that platform end to end — building the automations that drive memberships and supporting the owner and front-desk team who use it every day.

Culture: owner-led, fast-moving fitness business. Clear ownership, proactive communication, and steady improvement over perfection.

Role Details

  • Industry: Health & Fitness — Gym
  • Reports to: Gym Owner
  • Type: Full-time · 40 hours/week
  • Hours: US Eastern Time (EST) business hours
  • Rate: TBD
  • Location: Remote — Mexico
  • Tools: GoHighLevel (GHL), Zapier / Make / n8n, gym management software (e.g., Mindbody, ABC Glofox, PushPress, Zen Planner), Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Google Workspace

Role Overview

Every lead, trial, and member touchpoint at the gym runs through GoHighLevel. The GHL Specialist will design and maintain those systems — from the first ad inquiry to the membership renewal — and provide responsive, first-line support to the gym owner and staff.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move between building and supporting in the same day: fixing a broken trial-booking workflow in the morning, walking the front desk through the pipeline after lunch, and documenting both so it doesn't happen twice. The right person treats every support request as a signal of what to systematize next.

Key Responsibilities

GHL Automation & Build

  • Build and maintain lead nurture workflows — speed-to-lead SMS/email, trial class and intro session booking, and follow-up for leads who don't book
  • Automate the member journey — class and appointment reminders, no-show follow-up, new-member onboarding, and milestone check-ins
  • Run retention and reactivation campaigns — lapsed and frozen members, expiring memberships, failed payments, and win-back offers
  • Set up and manage pipelines, calendars, forms, surveys, landing pages/funnels, custom fields, and tags
  • Build and send email and SMS campaigns — promotions, challenges, events, and monthly member newsletters
  • Automate review requests and referral campaigns to grow the gym's reputation
  • Integrate GHL with the gym's management software, payment tools, and ad lead sources (Facebook/Instagram lead forms) via native integrations, Zapier, Make, n8n, or webhooks

Customer Support

  • Serve as first-line GHL support for the gym owner and front-desk/sales staff
  • Manage and respond to member and lead inquiries in the GHL Conversations inbox (SMS, email, social DMs) within agreed response times
  • Troubleshoot issues: broken workflows, failed sends, calendar sync errors, A2P/10DLC and email deliverability problems, integration failures
  • Train gym staff on using GHL — pipelines, conversations, booking, and reporting — through live walkthroughs and short recorded videos
  • Escalate billing, platform-level bugs, or out-of-scope requests to the gym owner with a clear summary

Reporting, Documentation & Improvement

  • Build dashboards that track leads, trial bookings, show rates, conversions to membership, and retention
  • Write SOPs and how-to guides for every recurring build and support issue
  • Audit the account for broken, duplicate, or unused workflows and recommend clean-up
  • Track recurring issues and propose automations or fixes that remove them at the source
  • Use AI tools to speed up campaign copy, troubleshooting, and documentation

Who Will Succeed

"Builds it right, explains it simply, and fixes the root cause — not just the ticket."

  • Has built real GHL automations for live businesses — ideally gyms, studios, or other membership businesses
  • Understands how a gym makes money: leads, trials, memberships, retention
  • Patient and clear with busy, non-technical owners and staff — explains a workflow without jargon
  • Systems thinker who documents as they go and hates fixing the same problem twice
  • Takes initiative — spots what is broken or missing and raises it before the owner does

Experience & Skills
